page: Amazon Web Services m5a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration flags, though newer extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are absent. The instance includes no local instance storage and operates with a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are zero GPUs provided.

Benchmark testing demonstrates a split between multithreaded capacity and single-core execution speed. Single-core performance falls into lower percentiles, scoring 728.0 on Geekbench and 590.89 on stress-ng, reflecting the legacy Zen microarchitecture and conservative 2.5 GHz clock rates. Compression metrics are similarly constrained, with single-threaded gzip logging 16.7 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 5.95 GB/sec. When scaling across all 16 vCPUs, throughput normalizes to average percentiles across Geekbench multi-core (4687.0) and PassMark CPU (12645.43), indicating stable parallel performance.

Memory bandwidth measurements highlight a dependency on cache tiers. Cached reads achieve 620.36 GB/sec, while larger uncached memory blocks drop to 30.35 GB/sec read and 15.02 GB/sec write. In database-centric evaluations, Redis SET operations reached 9.97 million operations per second, supported by average PassMark database ratings. Language model processing shows acceptable performance on small 135M parameter models (123.02 generation tokens/sec), but declines significantly when scaling to 7B parameter models (7.46 generation tokens/sec), illustrating limitations under compute-heavy memory-bound artificial intelligence tasks.

The AWS m5a.4xlarge presents a balanced cost-efficiency profile for standard multithreaded workloads that do not require modern vectorization extensions or peak single-thread frequency. Because it lacks bundled local storage, persistent disk operations rely on network-attached storage architectures. It serves as an effective host for multi-threaded backend web applications, relational databases, continuous integration build runners, and caching layers that benefit from its 64.0 GB memory pool.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.4xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor, offering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. Operating at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, it has no integrated GPUs and relies on remote storage, backed by a 5 Gbps baseline network. Benchmark evaluations show modest single-threaded performance offset by average multithreaded capacity across PassMark (12645.43) and Geekbench multi-core (4687.0). Memory subsystems deliver 620.36 GB/sec in cached reads alongside solid in-memory key-value processing, logging 9.97 million Redis SET operations per second. However, heavy data compression and uncached memory access show weaker execution metrics. It is well matched for mid-tier caching tiers, enterprise web applications, CI/CD runners, and general back-office data processing.
